youtube.title: Netflix vs Blockbuster: Netflix Bet $40 Million on Streaming Early
youtube.description:
Netflix vs Blockbuster is usually told as a simple story, but in January 2007 Netflix was still a DVD-by-mail business with about 1,000 streaming titles against 70,000 on DVD. Why would a profitable company start building the thing that could replace its own best product? This documentary follows how Netflix beat Blockbuster through the filings, the shareholder letters and Reed Hastings's own words, from the Roku box and the 2011 Qwikster split to a company with more than 300 million members.

This documentary follows the decision through the filings, the shareholder letters and Reed Hastings's own words: the browser player and the box it gave away to Roku, the rented libraries, the 2011 price split and Qwikster that together cost 800,000 US members in one quarter, and how the bet built a company with more than 300 million paid memberships.

youtube.comment: Netflix paid for streaming with its own DVD business. Which company today should be doing the same to itself? 👇

sources.claim: In January 2007 Netflix started streaming (Watch Now) to subscribers' PCs
The first streaming library held about 1,000 titles against 70,000 on DVD
Watch Now was rolled out over about six months, at no extra fee
One hour of streaming for each dollar of the monthly plan (18 hours on the $17.99 plan)
Watch Now required a Windows PC and Internet Explorer
Netflix expected to spend about $40 million on streaming in 2007
sources.source: Netflix Q4 2006 results, January 2007, as reported by The New York Times, 16 January 2007

sources.claim: Netflix earned $49 million net income in 2006
About 6.3 million subscribers at the end of 2006
Revenue of $997 million in 2006
A nationwide network of distribution centres delivering most discs within one business day
Blockbuster revenue of about $5.5 billion in 2006
Revenue of about $1.2 billion and about 7.5 million subscribers in 2007
Marc Randolph and Reed Hastings founded Netflix in California in 1997; DVD rentals by mail began in April 1998
sources.source: Marc Randolph, That Will Never Work (2019); Netflix company history

sources.claim: Monthly subscription plan with no late fees introduced in 1999
In 2000 the founders flew to Dallas and offered Blockbuster the company for $50 million; Blockbuster declined, and by Randolph's account its side struggled not to laugh
sources.source: Marc Randolph, That Will Never Work (2019)

sources.claim: Netflix listed on Nasdaq in May 2002 and posted its first full-year profit in 2003
sources.source: Netflix Form S-1 and IPO, May 2002; Netflix Form 10-K for fiscal 2003

sources.claim: Netflix delivered its one-billionth DVD in February 2007
Blockbuster launched Total Access in November 2006, letting mail customers return discs in stores
Netflix cut prices on its popular plans by $1 in July 2007
sources.source: Netflix Q2 2007 results and price announcement, July 2007

sources.claim: About 47% of American adults had home broadband in early 2007
sources.source: Pew Internet & American Life Project, Home Broadband Adoption 2007, June 2007

sources.claim: Apple began selling movies on iTunes in September 2006
Amazon launched Unbox video downloads in September 2006
Netflix built its own streaming box in-house and spun it out to Roku; reported reasoning was that its own hardware would deter other device makers
sources.source: Ken Auletta, 'Outside the Box', The New Yorker, 3 February 2014

sources.claim: The Netflix Player by Roku went on sale in May 2008 for $99.99
sources.source: Roku and Netflix press release, 20 May 2008

sources.claim: In January 2008 Netflix made streaming unlimited on most plans
Streaming reached the Xbox 360 in November 2008
Netflix arrived on PlayStation 3 in November 2009
Blockbuster's CEO: 'Neither RedBox nor Netflix are even on the radar screen in terms of competition.'
sources.source: Interview with Blockbuster CEO Jim Keyes, The Motley Fool, December 2008

sources.claim: Starz deal added about 2,500 films and shows in October 2008
sources.source: Netflix and Starz press release, 1 October 2008

sources.claim: By 2011, Netflix was reportedly paying Starz around $30 million a year
sources.source: Press reports on the Starz renewal talks, e.g. Reuters, 1 September 2011

sources.claim: Netflix signed with Epix in August 2010, reportedly for nearly $1 billion over five years
Starz said on 1 September 2011 it would not renew; deal ended February 2012
Blockbuster filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2010
sources.source: Blockbuster Inc. Chapter 11 petition, US Bankruptcy Court, S.D.N.Y., 23 September 2010

sources.claim: Netflix launched in Canada as streaming-only in September 2010
Streaming-only US plan at $7.99 a month from November 2010
About 20 million members at the end of 2010; Netflix described itself to shareholders as now primarily a streaming company
sources.source: Netflix letters to shareholders, Q3 2010 (20 October 2010) and Q4 2010 (26 January 2011)

sources.claim: On 12 July 2011 Netflix said treating DVDs as a $2 add-on to unlimited streaming no longer made financial sense
The combined plan was split, raising $9.99 to $15.98 (about 60%); streaming-only and DVD-only each $7.99
Qwikster announced 18 September 2011 with its own website, separate queues and separate card charges; dropped 10 October 2011
sources.source: Reed Hastings, Netflix blog, 18 September 2011; Netflix blog, 10 October 2011

sources.claim: 'I messed up. I owe everyone an explanation.'
sources.source: Reed Hastings, 'An Explanation and Some Reflections', Netflix blog, 18 September 2011

sources.claim: 'For the past five years, my greatest fear at Netflix has been that we wouldn't make the leap from success in DVDs to success in streaming.'
sources.source: Reed Hastings, 'An Explanation and Some Reflections', Netflix blog, 18 September 2011

sources.claim: 'Most companies that are great at something – like AOL dialup or Borders bookstores – do not become great at new things people want (streaming for us) because they are afraid to hurt their initial business.'
sources.source: Reed Hastings, 'An Explanation and Some Reflections', Netflix blog, 18 September 2011

sources.claim: US members fell from about 24.6 million (June 2011) to about 23.8 million (September 2011), a loss of about 800,000
sources.source: Netflix letters to shareholders, Q2 2011 (25 July 2011) and Q3 2011 (24 October 2011)

sources.claim: Netflix expected a consolidated loss in 2012 due to international expansion
sources.source: Netflix Q3 2011 letter to shareholders, 24 October 2011

sources.claim: Netflix shares fell roughly three-quarters between July and November 2011
Netflix raised $400 million in November 2011 through new shares and convertible notes
sources.source: Netflix Form 8-K and press release, 21 November 2011

sources.claim: End of 2011: about 21.7 million US streaming members and 11.2 million US DVD members
sources.source: Netflix Q4 2011 letter to shareholders, 25 January 2012

sources.claim: Global paid streaming memberships 2011-2024 (23.5M, 44.4M, 74.8M, 117.6M, 167.1M, 221.8M, 260.3M, 301.6M)
sources.source: Netflix quarterly letters to shareholders, Q4 2011 to Q4 2024

sources.claim: The DVD business reported its own profit to investors for years after the split
Netflix launched streaming-only in the UK and Ireland in January 2012
House of Cards premiered with all episodes on 1 February 2013
Netflix reportedly committed more than $100 million for two seasons of House of Cards without a pilot
On 6 January 2016 Netflix launched in 130 more countries, announced by Hastings at CES in Las Vegas
Netflix mailed its last DVDs on 29 September 2023 after more than five billion shipped
Hastings moved from co-CEO to executive chairman in January 2023
sources.source: Netflix Q4 2022 letter to shareholders, 19 January 2023

sources.claim: Dish Network bought Blockbuster's assets at a bankruptcy auction in April 2011 for about $320 million
sources.source: Dish Network press release and US Bankruptcy Court, S.D.N.Y., April 2011

sources.claim: Netflix revenue of about $39 billion in 2024
More than 301 million paid memberships at the end of 2024
sources.source: Netflix Q4 2024 letter to shareholders, 21 January 2025

sources.claim: The last Blockbuster store still open is a franchise in Bend, Oregon
